title: Interactive map with filtering, symbology and sharing
question: Can an AI agent turn a public dataset into a filtered, styled map I can share?
answer: Yes. The agent inspects the source, writes one map-v1 JSON object with the filter, renderer, basemap and camera, validates it, and returns a #map=json: link that opens the finished map. No account or server call is needed.
triggers: Map this data and color it by population
Filter these counties and make a choropleth I can share
Make one map colored by year and another by acreage, and give me two links

required.name: source
required.description: HTTPS URL of a public layer (or a sublayer index).

optional.name: where
optional.description: Read-only SQL attribute filter on real field names.

optional.name: renderer
optional.description: RendererSpec: simple, categories, choropleth, graduated-symbols, heatmap, or auto.

optional.name: basemap
optional.description: One of the map-v1 basemap ids.

optional.name: camera
optional.description: Center, zoom, tilt, heading, or fit to layers.

optional.name: outputs
optional.description: Link, QR card, Smart Map PNG, PDF.

steps.action: Read llms.txt, this recipe and api/capabilities.json; note the engine and execution environment you actually have.
Read the source metadata: geometry type, field names and types, spatial reference, extent, sentinels and query support. Query real values before filtering; never invent fields.

Choose the simplest level that can express the request: a ?layer= URL for one layer with a basic style; a map-v1 spec for categories, class breaks, colors, camera or several layers; the in-page API only to change a map already open. Keep attribute filters (where) separate from spatial ones.
Validate the spec and renderer against the real fields. Treat warnings as unfinished work.

Write the link: https://gismap.online/#map=json:<URI-encoded map-v1>. For follow-ups, decode the existing link (mapSpec.decode or mapSpec.fromShareParameters), clone it, change only what was asked, and write a new link per variant.
Open the link, wait for gisMapOnline.ready and the layers, then check describe().state.issues, layers.list() (loaded, feature count, renderer, where) and mapSpec.fromCurrent().
Return the actual link. Optional: a Smart Map PNG (smartImages.downloadCurrent) or the app's Map PDF and QR card (Share & export, in the UI).

artifact.structure: One map-v1 object: layers (url, where, renderer, opacity), basemap, skin, camera, legend.

outputs.format: Smart Map PNG (image with the project embedded)
outputs.notes: Keep the original file: image services and messengers can strip the embedded data. Remote layers are referenced, not embedded.
Made in the app with Share & export (no in-page method yet). A PDF is a static picture of the map.

verification: Source loaded with a nonzero feature count
Renderer type and field applied; legend shown
Share link reopens to the same spec (mapSpec.fromCurrent)
limitations: Readable #map=json: links are limited to 8,192 characters; use mapSpec.createLink for compressed links.
A year slider is not part of map-v1; use a timeline briefing for year-by-year playback.
Map PDF and map QR card have no in-page API; briefing.exportPdf and briefing.exportQrCard cover briefings.
recovery: If a field is missing, re-read ?f=pjson and use the exact name and case.
If validation warns about a renderer, the service style is used; fix the renderer rather than shipping the warning.
If a compressed link cannot be decoded in your environment, ask for the original JSON or a #map=json: link.
